practice_questions.question_text: An algorithm examines all n! orderings. Describe why buying a processor twice as fast does not remove its scalability problem as n grows,and state one memory-saving implementation choice.
practice_questions.adaptation_rationale: Retains factorial-workload/hardware tradeoff reasoning under explicit scalability/time-space scope;doesnotclassify theproblem asNP merelybecause enumeration isexpensive.
practice_questions.solution: The number of orderings grows factorially.; A factor-of-two speedup reduces a fixed run’s time but does not change that growth class.; Increasing n can therefore overwhelm the hardware improvement.; Generate/process one ordering at a time instead of storing all permutations simultaneously.

marking_points.criterion: The number of orderings grows factorially.
A factor-of-two speedup reduces a fixed run’s time but does not change that growth class.
Increasing n can therefore overwhelm the hardware improvement.
Generate/process one ordering at a time instead of storing all permutations simultaneously.
